analysis.title: GS Consumer: 5 Things We Are Watching Tonight
key_insights: Restaurants were the best consumer sub-sector on 10/28 at +3%, with some smaller caps up 9-11%. EAT and WING each rose about 12%. GS sees the move as driven more by positioning and WEN strategic headlines than by EAT/WING earnings, since small caps outperformed, and expects limited read-across.

EAT out-quarter comments were better than feared (high single-digit positive trends). WING 3Q same-store sales were -5.4%, soft but better than lower fears. GS says 4Q same-store sales remain the biggest focus in restaurants.

CMG beat 3Q and the stock is +3% after hours. 3Q comp was +2.1% vs consensus +1.5%. Investors will look for quarter-to-date trends, which have been the recent concern, and the reaction will help decide whether the group rally lasts.

SFM is -17% after a 4Q guide well below consensus: EPS guided 60% below and comp sales 400 bps below. GS says an EPS guide this far below is rare in grocery. The open question is whether the miss is SFM-specific or a grocery issue.

Investors had been somewhat less negative on grocery on a view that sticky inflation could give comp relief. SFM sentiment had remained weaker given the data. A downgrade of ACI last week drew more pushback than expected.

BOOT is -3% after hours on very little volume, after making fresh 1.5-year lows on 10/27. The out-quarter guide was tough but expected, about 250 bps below on revenue. The question is what is already priced in and whether other stocks take a cue from the reaction.

MGM had a challenging 3Q y/y in both Vegas and Macau, as expected. The release said October has rebounded favorably (Vegas). GS notes that several airlines also cited better 4Q revenue trends and concludes travel demand is holding up.
GS's desk was a better buyer of restaurant names on 10/28, and CMG was much better to buy ahead of the print.
